highlights.title: New Democratic Congress will likely strip the gilding from Trump's Golden Dome
highlights.summary: Two of the top lawmakers backing the Pentagon's Golden Dome missile defense shield are among the wave of Republicans leaving Congress in the coming Democratic takeover, raising questions about the future of President Donald Trump's signature second-term defense initiative.
body: The shakeup on Capitol Hill comes after military officials signaled in recent months that they might backpedal from one element Trump asked for in Golden Dome: the capability to shoot down missiles in their initial boost phase shortly after launch.

The Golden Dome has escaped serious congressional scrutiny since Trump announced the program in January 2025, one week into his second term in the White House. That lack of scrutiny will change as Democrats take responsibility for writing the Pentagon’s budget, introduce limits on funding, and put forth bills to strip out Golden Dome’s most controversial component and give the program a new name.

That’s the opinion of a half-dozen current and former officials in industry and government. Ars spoke with sources before and after last week’s congressional elections to get a sense of how a new Democratic Congress might make its imprint on missile defense.

highlights.title: Authors Can Defend Against AI Allegations With ‘Paper Trail’ Tools. Is It Enough?
highlights.summary: As the publishing industry wrestles with paranoia over the provenance of manuscripts, writers are caught in an impossible bind.
body: Andrea Bartz is a prolific novelist with an impressive résumé. Since 2019, she has published five thrillers, become a New York Times bestselling author, had her work optioned by the likes of Netflix and Hulu, and picked up an endorsement from Reese Witherspoon’s influential book club.

She also has a legal claim to fame: Bartz was the lead plaintiff in a class-action suit against Anthropic that alleged the company had downloaded millions of copyrighted books from pirate sites to use as training data for its models. Anthropic last year agreed to pay $1.5 billion in the largest copyright settlement in US history.

But while Bartz and many other writers were on guard against this plunder of their work, another AI threat was brewing. What happens when authors are accused of relying on artificial intelligence themselves?

highlights.title: Burn replaces injured Guehi in England squad
highlights.summary: Newcastle's Dan Burn is added to the England squad to play Croatia and Spain in the Nations League this week after Marc Guehi pulls out with a hip injury.
body: Newcastle's Dan Burn has been added to the England squad to play Croatia and Spain in the Nations League this week after Manchester City defender Marc Guehi pulled out with a hip injury.
Guehi was substituted at half-time of City's loss at Nottingham Forest on Saturday and manager Enzo Maresca said afterwards the centre-back had requested to come off because of the injury.
BBC Sport revealed on Sunday that the 26-year-old was having a scan to determine the severity of the ongoing issue, and the defender has now been ruled out of this week's matches.
The former Crystal Palace captain has been a mainstay of Thomas Tuchel's team since his appointment as England head coach in January 2025.

highlights.title: Mass Effect Creator Is ‘Optimistic’ the Series Will Live On
highlights.summary: BioWare's shutdown has been one of the hardest studio closures in gaming history. The Edmonton-based studio made its way into thousands of gamers' hearts, and it was set to continue this mission with the development of Mass Effect Universe, the next entry in the Mass Effect series.
body: In 2020, in celebration of N7 Day, the annual celebration of the Mass Effect franchise, BioWare announced that it was working on a new Mass Effect game, but it was only in the early stages of development. Besides a handful of teasers, not much was heard about the project from then on. When private investors bought EA, Mass Effect 5 seemed increasingly unlikely. Unfortunately, that proved true: EA shut down BioWare and canceled the project on Oct. 21, 2026, nearly six years after its announcement.

However, neither fans nor developers were ready to give up on Mass Effect just yet. Petitions were created, billboards were put up to raise awareness, voice actors showed support, and developers even leaked an early trailer to fuel the fire. The community has come together, celebrating N7 Day in a uniquely special way.

highlights.title: My son’s back home – and my mothering skills have gone out of the window | Emma Beddington
highlights.summary: Like many graduates, he has been forced to return to the nest. How will he cope with my pigeon chat and dodgy dregs for dinner? My graduate son has been back home for five months now.
body: Well, I can still wash, dry and fold multiple loads a week and ensure an uninterrupted supply of milk. It’s muscle memory, instinctive as breathing. I’ve lost other skills, though, like deciding what’s for dinner. I quit cooking the minute we dropped him off in halls in 2022 and wasn’t expecting to get my guns (guns = repertoire of five Meera Sodha recipes) out again. My husband and I have lost our conversational skills too, conversing in rambling, repetitive shorthand, and it’s unnerving having someone around to notice how much we talk about pigeons (constantly).
Of course, when he does escape, as older friends remind me, if I’m lucky I might get another last job after this last job: grandparenting.

highlights.title: Instagram’s AI age detection is expanding globally
highlights.summary: Meta is globally expanding the age estimation technology it uses to find teenagers on Instagram who haven't correctly disclosed their age. The rollout will automatically place "millions more teens on Instagram into Teen Account protections," according to Meta's announcement, after launching the…
body: Meta says it will expand Teen Account protections to millions more kids, even if they’ve misrepresented their age.

The age detection tools proactively look for signals that likely determine whether Instagram users are under 18 years old, such as the other profiles and types of content they interact with, birthday messages they receive, and “general themes and visual cues” from uploaded photos and videos, including height and bone structure. Meta says that it’s also started using Apple’s age-range signal as an additional detection method in Australia.

The age assurance system is used to remove Instagram users who are believed to be under 13 (the minimum age required for Meta social accounts), and automatically place users between 13-17 under more restrictive Teen Accounts, even if they signed up using a fake adult birthday. Teen Accounts are designed to provide a safer and more age-appropriate experience by being private by default, limiting what kind of content teens can see, and preventing strangers from sending them DMs.

highlights.title: Bikers and Bug-Lovers Join Forces to Fight a New Google Data Center
highlights.summary: As data center protests break out across Europe, a mismatched band of campaigners is trying to block Google from building a sprawling new facility east of London.
body: On Wednesday afternoon, Jamie Robins strolled up to the entrance of Google’s UK headquarters in Kings Cross, London. He brandished a letter containing details of a petition signed by almost 55,000 people, calling for Google to abandon plans to build a large new data center in Thurrock, 15 miles to the east of London.

Robins works for wildlife conservation trust Buglife, part of an unlikely alliance of special-interest groups trying to block the Thurrock development. Buglife and local wildlife groups fear for an endangered plant, rare bumblebee, and other invertebrates whose habitat they say will be destroyed. Nonprofit Foxglove says the data center will emit too much pollution. The Thurrock Hammers motorcycle club wants to return to racing on the site.
Members of the various groups joined Robins outside Google’s office last Wednesday, holding placards demanding the company “search elsewhere” for somewhere to put its facility.

highlights.title: Dungeons in World of Warcraft: Forever get a huge XP buff, but power-levellers shouldn't celebrate just yet
highlights.summary: World of Warcraft: Forever has received a massive buff to the XP drop-rates of dungeon mobs (enemies), which should make running these instances multiple times feel more rewarding - and may revive an older levelling strategy.
body: This buff is a 50 percent increase in experience from all mobs killed inside all dungeons. As detailed in this World of Warcraft forum post, community manager Kaivax wrote that this change has been made "so it feels better to go back in for more runs". They don't outright say this is in response to community feedback, but the subject has been a hot topic since the beta.

World of Warcraft: Forever developers have spoken in the past about the decision to deliberately bring down dungeon mob XP to disincentivise power-levelling in dungeons. The idea was that by doing this, people would be encouraged to actually go out into the world and explore it, rather than hopping from instance to instance until they reached max level.

Sadly, a side effect of this change is that doing a dungeon more than once could feel unrewarding. Playing it once is great, as you get to complete lots of quests that reward guaranteed items and XP. However, if you go back again, you don't get these, so your only source of progression comes from a heavily decreased XP rate.

highlights.title: The pet I’ll never forget: Mae the labrador, who keeps me safe with her keen nose and piercing stare
highlights.summary: Before getting her, I would fall, injure myself and then wake up alone. I’ve trained Mae to be a medical alert dog and she has helped me to embrace life again. It was love at first sight. I met Mae, a black labrador, in 2023 when she was 11 weeks old and she melted my heart completely.
body: At the time I was struggling with the physical and mental symptoms of my illnesses and needed a medical alert dog but there was a long waiting list. So I decided to train my own dog with the help of the Medical Detection Dogs charity.

Before Mae I would fall, injure myself and then wake up alone. Now Mae can tell based on my smell that a medical episode – when my heart rate drastically increases, causing me to pass out – is coming. She recognises my odour when I’m unwell and is given a treat so sees it as a fun activity. She alerts me either by giving me a very intense stare, or if I’ve missed that because my back is turned, she will escalate the alert by doing a very gentle jump up. She has even adapted her alerts to stare at whoever has got her lead so that they can tell me to take action.

If she’s feeling particularly cheeky when I come around after an episode, she’ll fetch her treat pot and toys so I can play with her, which is also quite relaxing. I can’t put into words how magical and calming it is to have this gorgeous dog staring at you and I think to myself: “I’m really lucky to have her in my life.”

highlights.title: New Hulu Doc ‘Get Huge’ Shows the Deadly Toll of Looksmaxxing
highlights.summary: The new Hulu docuseries Get Huge: Looksmaxxing to Death shines a light on the mysterious deaths and disappearances of a group of male influencers in Thailand—and the leader at the center of it all.
body: Before Clavicular, before Androgenic, before the Tate brothers, before bonesmashing and frame-mogging and the manosphere and looksmaxxing entered the online lexicon, there was Tony Huge.

A 44-year-old former model turned lawyer turned bodybuilder turned supplement impresario, Huge fled the United States for Thailand to escape legal pressure on his company from the Food and Drug Administration and to build out a “harem” of young, nubile Thai women. With his bulky frame, his sex-and-drugs-fueled lifestyle, and his motto “a day natty [natural] is a day wasted,” Huge became an icon for what was then the fledgling biohacking community. He amassed a huge following of disaffected, lonely young men, some of whom moved to Thailand to live with him. Then, some of them started dying.

Huge is one of the main focuses of Get Huge: Looksmaxxing to Death, a bone-chilling documentary series hitting Hulu on November 10. Directed by Stacey Lee and executive-produced by the journalist Jennings Brown, Get Huge kicks off with the untimely death of “Leo and Longevity,” aka Laith Abdallah Algaz, a biohacker and penis enlargement influencer who was found deceased in Huge’s home in January 2023.

highlights.title: A single AI model simulates the behavior of many substances, from sliding sand to folding proteins
highlights.summary: By learning how matter moves, the WorldParticle system could assist with developing soft robots, medicines, and more.
body: Today, a scientist who wants to simulate a physical process must pick the right tool for that one job, such as a solver built for flowing water or another designed to model the way a protein folds. Each one is hand-coded around the specific equations that dictate how that process behaves.

Researchers at MIT, the University of British Columbia (UBC), and elsewhere have now replaced that patchwork with a single deep-learning system, called WorldParticle, that could help engineers model different physical phenomena, from sliding sand to folding proteins, with one unified artificial intelligence architecture.

Scientists and engineers could use this system to model processes that typically require separate simulators, such as a fluid sloshing against a deformable solid. This could offer a faster, more accurate way to simulate how sloshing oil might impact an elastic valve in a storage tank, for instance. It could also help engineers study where and how granular materials, like sand or soil, could move when a soft robot touches them.
points: By learning how matter moves, the WorldParticle system could assist with developing soft robots, medicines, and more.

highlights.title: WoW: Forever Boosts Dungeon XP As Blizzard Struggles to Get Leveling Balance Right
highlights.summary: Blizzard just gave some ground in its battle to get players to slow down and spend more time in the open world in World of Warcraft: Forever.
body: The developer applied a hotfix on Sunday that boosted experience points (XP) for killing monsters in dungeons by 50%. It's Blizzard's first concession to complaints from players that dungeons, a core part of the WoW experience, had become too unrewarding to play compared to questing in the open world.

Blizzard is struggling to find the sweet spot for leveling in WoW: Forever. The intention is that leveling in Forever should be faster and smoother than it was in classic WoW (which is definitely the case), but that the journey to level 60 should still feel substantial. Additionally, Blizzard is keen to promote the open-world questing experience and avoid players spending all their time running dungeons just to race to the finish line.

When the beta began, XP from killing monsters in dungeons was heavily reduced compared to WoW Classic, while XP for completing dungeon quests was dramatically increased — the idea being that dungeons would be worth running once, but after that, you'd return to questing.
points: Blizzard just gave some ground in its battle to get players to slow down and spend more time in the open world in World of Warcraft: Forever.

highlights.title: AI-assisted learning platform helps robots reason beyond literal commands
highlights.summary: The new approach, known as FLEX, could lead to more intuitive, interactive household and assistive robots.
body: Images for download on the MIT News office website are made available to non-commercial entities, press and the general public under a Creative Commons Attribution Non-Commercial No Derivatives license. You may not alter the images provided, other than to crop them to size. A credit line must be used when reproducing images; if one is not provided below, credit the images to "MIT."

Humans are intuitive by nature. We can sense meaning beyond the literal words that we encounter. Now, a new artificial intelligence-assisted learning platform developed by MIT engineers is enabling robots to read larger meaning into a human’s natural language commands.

In a study to be presented at the annual Conference on Robot Learning this month, researchers from MIT and New York University introduce FLEX, a flexible feature-editing pipeline for robot motion-planning.

With FLEX, humans can interact with a robot by giving it instructions in natural, conversational language. The robot can not only follow the instructions literally but also read into the words to draw larger generalizations that help to improve its motion-planning task.

highlights.title: Neville: Is Man City charges spotlight seeping into performances?
highlights.summary: Gary Neville has questioned whether the recent attention over Manchester City being charged by the Premier League has begun to seep into the team's performances.
body: The club were found guilty of 114 serious breaches of the Premier League's financial rules in September. Man City deny all the charges and have lodged an appeal against the verdict. No sanctions have yet been announced.
However, Enzo Maresca's side have now lost their last three matches in the Premier League, including a 3-1 defeat to Nottingham Forest at the weekend.

body: “I’ve spent the last 25 years of my career trying to re-create that experience,” Smith says of the WB teen drama, on which he played the sensitive jock Jack McPhee for five seasons. “I’ve been trying to measure up to it my entire career.”

Speaking on a Zoom call this October, Smith is now 53, gray-haired and hatted with a brisk demeanor, Smith revisits that pursuit in his new memoir, I Don’t Want to Wait: My Life on Dawson’s Creek. Part oral history and part personal reckoning, the book draws on conversations with former castmates and colleagues, including big-hitters like Katie Holmes, to revisit the series, the protests that followed Jack’s coming-out storyline, and an episode of homophobic harassment Smith had never previously discussed. Highly rhapsodic and wistful about his experience on Dawson’s Creek, Kerr fully embraces the nostalgia in the memoir.

highlights.title: Is it true that … dock leaves cure nettle stings?
highlights.summary: It’s a time-honoured treatment and rubbing certainly helps, but other leaves could be just as good. If you’ve ever brushed against a stinging nettle, chances are someone told you to find a dock leaf.
body: Probably not in any way that’s unique to the plant, says John Tregoning, a professor at Imperial College London and the author of Live Forever? A Curious Scientist’s Guide to Wellness, Ageing and Death.

When you brush against a nettle, tiny hairs on the plant can pierce the skin and release a mixture of chemicals, including histamine, acetylcholine and serotonin. These trigger burning, itching and redness.

Could dock leaves contain chemicals that counteract the sting, such as antihistamines? “Maybe, but probably not,” says Tregoning. There is little evidence that dock leaf sap contains substances capable of significantly relieving the reaction.

So why do people swear by them? Rubbing a leaf against the skin may provide a competing sensation that temporarily distracts from the pain, says Tregoning. “There’s a limit to the number of sensations that the nerve cells can process, so if you overstimulate them with the rubbing there’s less feedback from the pain.”

When I was studying electrical engineering in India in the 1980s, a professor asked our class: “Why do short- and medium-wave radios produce a crackling sound, or static, when a scooter goes past, regardless of the station you are listening to?” None of us knew the answer.

The professor was using the question to introduce a mathematical operation called a Fourier transform. Each time the spark plug in a scooter engine fires, it produces a short pulse of electromagnetic radiation. The Fourier transform reveals that, mathematically, this signal is a summation of thousands of sine and cosine waves. Whatever frequency our radios are tuned to, the pulse produced by the spark plug contains some energy at that frequency, which we hear as static. It was a proverbial ‘aha’ moment for many of us in the class.

body: The announcement, shared on Oct. 8 at the Spy x Family Anime Extra Mission II special event and on the official Spy x Family website, came as a pleasant surprise for fans. Season 3 of the anime aired from October to December 2025, exactly two years after season 2 ended. If the timeframe remains consistent, fans can expect season 4 to air at the end of 2027. The franchise's second movie will come out in the same year, following the success of Spy x Family's first outing in cinemas, Spy x Family Code: White, released in 2023.

The series' comedy stems from three people living together while hiding their true identities. Airheaded Anya is one of the most adorable characters in anime, while Loid and Yor's marriage of convenience is slowly (too slowly!) developing into a real romance. Seeing this dynamic built on lies grow into a real found family is truly heartwarming, but Spy x Family hides a much more serious side. The themes of war and violence are never treated dismissively, and the series has delivered some of the best reflections on the topic seen in the medium.

highlights.title: The hill I will die on: Nobody just ‘rustles up’ a lasagne | Keren Levy
highlights.summary: We need to give up this pretence of effortlessness and start calling the dish what it is: a laborious meat-and-cheese architecture project. What is this “rustling up a lasagne” thing – apart from a straightforward contradiction?
body: I have a clear memory of the moment when, only recently out of our student years, a friend first pulled this misrepresentation out of her hungover hat. It was the day after a party, with a big clear-up under way and an agreed need for carbs. There was exhaustion, there were bin liners in hands, but she was busy “rustling”. And then, a mere few hours of laborious cooking and construction later, there it was on the table: the absolutely standard lasagne, in its “oh this old thing” white baking dish.

Decades later, the sheet-pasta extravaganza retains its reputation as an effortless standby, despite involving multiple components, careful assembly and a baking time long enough to watch a Netflix episode. You could be at the office picnic, an “everyone bring a course” dinner, even a wake, and people will casually announce they’ve made a lasagne as if they’ve decided to boil an egg, not committed hours to a meat-and-cheese architecture project.

“It’s no bother,” they add. “You can even buy the ready-made pasta sheets and do the cheat’s version. You don’t have to make it from scratch.” The relief. You’re still building the house, but someone’s delivered some bricks.
